newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss to join new IMF emergency fund NAB.
newsitem.headline: Swiss to join new IMF emergency fund NAB.

text.p: Switzerland, a member of the Group of 10 (G10) leading industrial nations, will participate in the New Arrangements to Borrow (NAB), the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) new war chest to combat global financial crises.

The Swiss government on Wednesday asked the parliament to approve an 2.8 billion Swiss franc ($1.9 billion) increase in the credit line, which the IMF can draw upon in cases where a country's economic problems are so severe they may spill over to the global monetary system.
Switzerland's part of the $48 billion NAB is 4.6 percent and the participation does not burden the federal budget, the finance ministry said in a statement.
NAB was approved by IMF's executive board in January and doubles the amount of money available to IMF in an emergency.

In 1964 Switzerland became an associate member and in 1984 a full member of the General Arrangements to Borrow (GAB). Under GAB the 11 members of the G1O group make funds available to IMF for currency crises. GAB has not been activated since 1983.

Mexico's financial crises in late 1994 showed that GAB, some $25 billion in credit, was not large enough to handle the growing capital and trade volumes and IMF members decided to double the emergency funds.
NAB runs parallel to GAB and depending on the type of crises, IMF can draw on either credit line, the ministry said.
About 25 countries have pledged to join NAB.
